records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה בֹּ֖א אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֑ה כִּֽי־אֲנִ֞י הִכְבַּ֤דְתִּי אֶת־לִבּוֹ֙ וְאֶת־לֵ֣ב עֲבָדָ֔יו לְמַ֗עַן שִׁתִ֛י אֹתֹתַ֥י אֵ֖לֶּה בְּקִרְבּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, go in to Pharaoh, for I have made heavy his heart and [the] heart of his servants, so that I may set these signs of mine in his midst,
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Go in to Pharaoh. It is I who have hardened his heart and the hearts of his officials, in order to set these signs of {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}} right among them,

L.1: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Go in to Pharaoh, for I have made his heart heavy and the heart of his servants, so that I may set these signs of {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}} in his midst,

R.1: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Go to Pharaoh. I have made him and his officials stubborn. I did this so that I could do these mighty signs among them.

decisions.choice: I have made his heart heavy: God is the subject
decisions.reason: Pharaoh made his own heart heavy in 8:11, 28 and 9:34, he and his servants. Now God says that he has done it, with the same verb. See the note on 7:3 for the three verbs used for Pharaoh's heart.

decisions.choice: so that I may set these signs: God's purpose in the plagues
decisions.reason: The plagues are "signs" that show who Yahweh is (7:3-5). They are set "in his midst", among Pharaoh and his people. The purpose continues in verse 2.

decisions.choice: hardened his heart / made him stubborn
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "made his heart heavy" to show the Hebrew verb. Balanced says "hardened", Readable "stubborn", as in 8:11, 28.

records.heading: A warning of locusts

records.source: וּלְמַ֡עַן תְּסַפֵּר֩ בְּאָזְנֵ֨י בִנְךָ֜ וּבֶן־בִּנְךָ֗ אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁ֤ר הִתְעַלַּ֨לְתִּי֙ בְּמִצְרַ֔יִם וְאֶת־אֹתֹתַ֖י אֲשֶׁר־שַׂ֣מְתִּי בָ֑ם וִֽידַעְתֶּ֖ם כִּי־אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: and so that you may recount in [the] ears of your son and [the] son of your son how I have made a fool of Egypt, and my signs which I have set among them; and you will know that I [am] Yahweh.
pieces: and so that you can tell {{gender:your children and grandchildren|your sons and grandsons}} the story of how I made a mockery of Egypt, and of the signs I set among them. And you will all know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

L.2: and so that you may tell in the ears of {{gender:your child and your child's child|your son and your son's son}} how I have made a fool of Egypt, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} signs that I have set among them; and you will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

R.2: I also did it so that you can tell {{gender:your children and grandchildren|your sons and grandsons}} how I made fools of the Egyptians. You will tell them about the signs I did among them. Then you will all know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

decisions.choice: made a fool of: toyed with, dealt mockingly with
decisions.reason: The verb means to treat someone as a plaything, mocking or abusing them. Balaam says his donkey has "made a fool of" him (Numbers 22:29); Saul fears the Philistines will "abuse" him (1 Samuel 31:4); and the Philistines recall that God "dealt ruthlessly" with Egypt in these plagues (1 Samuel 6:6). It may stress the mockery of Egypt's power or the severity of what God did.

decisions.choice: in the ears of your son and your son's son: tell it to the generations to come
decisions.reason: Exodus tells parents to explain these events to their children (12:26-27; 13:8, 14). "Son" here means any child or descendant.

decisions.choice: you will know: all Israel will know
decisions.reason: "Tell" is addressed to Moses as one person, but "you will know" is plural. Pharaoh has been told he will know Yahweh (7:17; 8:6, 18); now Israel will know him too, as God promised in 6:7.

decisions.choice: I also did it so that
decisions.reason: Readable ends verse 1 with a full stop, so it repeats the start of the purpose clause here.

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֨א מֹשֶׁ֣ה וְאַהֲרֹן֮ אֶל־פַּרְעֹה֒ וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֵלָ֗יו כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י הָֽעִבְרִ֔ים עַד־מָתַ֣י מֵאַ֔נְתָּ לֵעָנֹ֖ת מִפָּנָ֑י שַׁלַּ֥ח עַמִּ֖י וְיַֽעַבְדֻֽנִי׃
records.gloss: And went Moses and Aaron to Pharaoh and said to him, thus says Yahweh, [the] God of the Hebrews, until when have you refused to humble yourself before me? Let go my people, that they may serve me.
pieces: So Moses and Aaron went in to Pharaoh and told him, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of the Hebrews, says this: 'How long will you go on refusing to bow before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? Release {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, so that they can serve {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

L.3: And Moses and Aaron went in to Pharaoh and said to him, "Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of the Hebrews: 'How long will you refuse to humble yourself before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? Let {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people go, that they may serve {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

R.3: So Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh. They said to him, "Here is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of the Hebrews, says: 'How much longer will you be too proud to give in to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? Let {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people go so they can worship {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: humble yourself: bow down, submit
decisions.reason: The verb is from the root used of Egypt "oppressing" Israel (1:11-12). Pharaoh, who humbled Israel, will not humble himself before God.

decisions.choice: how long have you refused: you have refused and still refuse
decisions.reason: The verb looks back over Pharaoh's refusals so far (4:23; 7:14, 27; 9:2) and asks how long they will go on.

decisions.choice: the God of the Hebrews: the name Pharaoh was first given
decisions.reason: God told Moses to use this title before Pharaoh (3:18), and Moses used it in 5:3; 7:16; 9:1, 13.

decisions.choice: worship
decisions.reason: The verb means both "serve" and "worship". Readable says "worship" here, as in 7:16, 26, since Moses asks to go and hold a festival.

decisions.choice: too proud to give in
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what refusing to humble oneself means.

records.source: כִּ֛י אִם־מָאֵ֥ן אַתָּ֖ה לְשַׁלֵּ֣חַ אֶת־עַמִּ֑י הִנְנִ֨י מֵבִ֥יא מָחָ֛ר אַרְבֶּ֖ה בִּגְבֻלֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: For if refusing [are] you to let go my people, look, I [am] bringing tomorrow locust[s] into your territory.
pieces: If you refuse to release {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, then tomorrow I will bring locusts across your borders.

L.4: For if you refuse to let {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people go, look, I am bringing locusts into your territory tomorrow.

R.4: If you still will not let {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people go, tomorrow I will send swarms of locusts into your land.

decisions.choice: locusts: the swarming locust
decisions.reason: This is the common word for the locust that travels in great swarms. Such swarms can strip a whole region of its plants (Joel 1:4; Psalm 105:34-35).

decisions.choice: look, I am bringing: the plague is about to happen
decisions.reason: The form describes something on the point of happening, and "tomorrow" fixes the time, as with the hail (9:18).

records.source: וְכִסָּה֙ אֶת־עֵ֣ין הָאָ֔רֶץ וְלֹ֥א יוּכַ֖ל לִרְאֹ֣ת אֶת־הָאָ֑רֶץ וְאָכַ֣ל׀אֶת־יֶ֣תֶר הַפְּלֵטָ֗ה הַנִּשְׁאֶ֤רֶת לָכֶם֙ מִן־הַבָּרָ֔ד וְאָכַל֙ אֶת־כָּל־הָעֵ֔ץ הַצֹּמֵ֥חַ לָכֶ֖ם מִן־הַשָּׂדֶֽה׃
records.gloss: And it will cover the eye of the land, and not anyone will be able to see the land; and it will eat the rest of the escaped [part] that remains to you from the hail, and it will eat every tree that sprouts for you from the field.
pieces: They will blanket the face of the land until no one can see the ground. They will consume whatever the hail spared, all that you still have left, and they will feed on every tree of yours that grows in the open country.

L.5: And they will cover the eye of the land, and no one will be able to see the land; and they will eat the rest of what escaped, what is left to you from the hail, and they will eat every tree of yours that sprouts from the field.

R.5: There will be so many locusts that no one will be able to see the ground. They will eat everything the hail did not destroy. They will eat the leaves off all your trees out in the fields.

decisions.choice: the eye of the land: the surface of the ground, all that can be seen
decisions.reason: The same phrase is used in verse 15 and in Numbers 22:5, 11, where Moab says Israel "covers the eye of the land".

decisions.choice: what escaped from the hail: the crops left after the seventh plague
decisions.reason: The hail destroyed the flax and barley but not the wheat and spelt, which had not yet come up (9:31-32). The locusts will finish what the hail began.

decisions.choice: it will cover: the swarm as one body
decisions.reason: The verbs are singular, treating the locusts as a single mass, as in verses 12-15.

decisions.choice: the face of the land / the ground
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew "eye". Balanced says "face", Readable "the ground".

decisions.choice: There will be so many locusts that
decisions.reason: Readable says why no one will see the ground.

records.source: וּמָלְא֨וּ בָתֶּ֜יךָ וּבָתֵּ֣י כָל־עֲבָדֶיךָ֮ וּבָתֵּ֣י כָל־מִצְרַיִם֒ אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹֽא־רָא֤וּ אֲבֹתֶ֨יךָ֙ וַאֲב֣וֹת אֲבֹתֶ֔יךָ מִיּ֗וֹם הֱיוֹתָם֙ עַל־הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה עַ֖ד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה וַיִּ֥פֶן וַיֵּצֵ֖א מֵעִ֥ם פַּרְעֹֽה׃
records.gloss: And they will fill your houses and [the] houses of all your servants and [the] houses of all Egypt, which not saw your fathers and [the] fathers of your fathers from [the] day of their being on the ground until this day. And he turned and went out from with Pharaoh.
pieces: Your houses will be full of them, and so will the houses of all your officials and of all the Egyptians. It will be a sight your ancestors never saw, neither your fathers nor their fathers, in all the time they have lived on this soil.'" Then Moses turned and went out from Pharaoh's presence.

L.6: And they will fill your houses and the houses of all your servants and the houses of all Egypt, [such] as your fathers and your fathers' fathers have not seen from the day they were on the ground until this day.'" And he turned and went out from Pharaoh.

R.6: They will fill your houses and the houses of your officials and of all the Egyptians. Nothing like this has happened since your people first lived in this land, not in your parents' time or your grandparents' time.'" Then Moses turned around and left Pharaoh.

decisions.choice: your fathers and your fathers' fathers: your ancestors for generations
decisions.reason: Nothing in Egypt's memory will compare. The same is said of the hail (9:18, 24) and of the locusts again in verse 14.

decisions.choice: he turned and went out: Moses
decisions.reason: The subject is not named, but it is Moses, with Aaron (verse 3). He leaves without waiting for Pharaoh's answer.

decisions.choice: Moses
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Moses; Literal keeps "he".

records.source: וַיֹּאמְרוּ֩ עַבְדֵ֨י פַרְעֹ֜ה אֵלָ֗יו עַד־מָתַי֙ יִהְיֶ֨ה זֶ֥ה לָ֨נוּ֙ לְמוֹקֵ֔שׁ שַׁלַּח֙ אֶת־הָ֣אֲנָשִׁ֔ים וְיַֽעַבְד֖וּ אֶת־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֑ם הֲטֶ֣רֶם תֵּדַ֔ע כִּ֥י אָבְדָ֖ה מִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And said [the] servants of Pharaoh to him, until when will be this [man] to us for a snare? Let go the men, that they may serve Yahweh their God. Not yet do you know that has perished Egypt?
pieces: Pharaoh's officials said to him, "How long must this man be a trap for us? Let the men go and serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God. Have you still not grasped that Egypt is lost?"

L.7: And the servants of Pharaoh said to him, "How long will this [man] be a snare to us? Let the men go, that they may serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God. Do you not yet know that Egypt is ruined?"

R.7: Pharaoh's officials said to him, "How much longer will this man cause us trouble? Let the men go to worship {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God. Egypt is already destroyed! Do you not see that?"

decisions.choice: snare: a trap, a cause of ruin
decisions.reason: The word is a bait or trap that catches an animal. Israel is warned that the gods of Canaan would be a snare to them (23:33; 34:12). "This" is most likely Moses; it may be the whole affair.

decisions.choice: the men: the Israelite men, perhaps the people as a whole
decisions.reason: This is the ordinary word for men, and it is sometimes used of the people of a group in general. The officials may mean the whole people. But Pharaoh's offer in verse 11, which lets only the men go, may take up their advice.

decisions.choice: Egypt is ruined: has perished, is as good as lost
decisions.reason: The verb is in the form for something already done: the officials speak of Egypt's ruin as a fact.

decisions.choice: the men
decisions.reason: "The men" has no gender setting, because the officials may mean the men only (see the meaning decision).

decisions.choice: worship
decisions.reason: As in verse 3.

records.source: וַיּוּשַׁ֞ב אֶת־מֹשֶׁ֤ה וְאֶֽת־אַהֲרֹן֙ אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֔ה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֔ם לְכ֥וּ עִבְד֖וּ אֶת־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֑ם מִ֥י וָמִ֖י הַהֹלְכִֽים׃
records.gloss: And was brought back Moses and Aaron to Pharaoh, and he said to them, go, serve Yahweh your God; who and who [are] the ones going?
pieces: Moses and Aaron were brought back to Pharaoh, who said to them, "Go and serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. But exactly who will be going?"

L.8: And Moses and Aaron were brought back to Pharaoh, and he said to them, "Go, serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. Who and who are the ones going?"

R.8: So Moses and Aaron were brought back to Pharaoh. He said to them, "Go and worship {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. But which of your people will go?"

decisions.choice: who and who: exactly which people
decisions.reason: The doubled question asks for a full list. Pharaoh grants the request only to start bargaining over who may go.

decisions.choice: was brought back: someone brought them
decisions.reason: The verb is passive; the officials of verse 7 most likely had them fetched.

decisions.choice: worship
decisions.reason: As in verse 3.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֔ה בִּנְעָרֵ֥ינוּ וּבִזְקֵנֵ֖ינוּ נֵלֵ֑ךְ בְּבָנֵ֨ינוּ וּבִבְנוֹתֵ֜נוּ בְּצֹאנֵ֤נוּ וּבִבְקָרֵ֨נוּ֙ נֵלֵ֔ךְ כִּ֥י חַג־יְהוָ֖ה לָֽנוּ׃
records.gloss: And said Moses, with our young and with our old we will go, with our sons and with our daughters, with our flock[s] and with our herd[s] we will go, for [a] festival of Yahweh [is] to us.
pieces: Moses said, "Young and old alike, we will go. Our sons and daughters will go, and our flocks and herds too, for we are holding a festival of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

L.9: And Moses said, "With our young and with our old we will go; with our sons and with our daughters, with our flocks and with our herds we will go, for it is a festival of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for us."

R.9: Moses said, "Everyone will go, young and old. Our sons and daughters will go. We will take our sheep, goats, and cattle. This is a festival for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and it is for all of us."

decisions.choice: our young and our old: everyone, of every age
decisions.reason: Naming the two ends of life includes all between. Moses then names sons and daughters and the animals: no one and nothing will stay behind.

decisions.choice: festival: a pilgrimage feast
decisions.reason: The word is used of a feast to which people travel, as in 5:1 and of Israel's three yearly feasts (23:14-17). The whole community keeps it.

decisions.choice: sheep, goats, and cattle
decisions.reason: Flocks were sheep and goats, herds were cattle. Readable names them.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֗ם יְהִ֨י כֵ֤ן יְהוָה֙ עִמָּכֶ֔ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר אֲשַׁלַּ֥ח אֶתְכֶ֖ם וְאֶֽת־טַפְּכֶ֑ם רְא֕וּ כִּ֥י רָעָ֖ה נֶ֥גֶד פְּנֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And he said to them, may be so Yahweh with you as I let go you and your little ones. See, for evil [is] before your faces.
pieces: Pharaoh said to them, "So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} be with you, just as surely as I will let you go with your little ones! Plainly you are plotting harm.

L.10: And he said to them, "So may {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} be with you, as I let you and your little ones go! See, for evil is before your faces.

R.10: Pharaoh mocked them. "Oh yes, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will be with you, just as surely as I will let you take your children along! You are plainly planning something evil.

decisions.choice: so may Yahweh be with you, as I let you go: a mocking wish meaning "I will never let you go"
decisions.reason: Pharaoh uses the form of a blessing in scorn. Yahweh will be with them as much as Pharaoh will let their children go, that is, not at all.

decisions.choice: evil is before your faces: you have harm in mind
alternatives: a play on the name of the god Ra
decisions.reason: Pharaoh most likely accuses them of an evil purpose: they mean to escape for good. The words can also be a threat, "disaster lies ahead of you". Some have heard in the word "evil" a play on the name of the Egyptian sun god Ra, as if Pharaoh said his god stood against them; that is possible but cannot be shown.

decisions.choice: little ones: children and others who could not travel alone
decisions.reason: The word means young children and sometimes all the dependents of a household (Genesis 47:12).

decisions.choice: Pharaoh mocked them
decisions.reason: Readable says that the wish is scornful, since a plain reading would sound like a blessing.

records.source: לֹ֣א כֵ֗ן לְכֽוּ־נָ֤א הַגְּבָרִים֙ וְעִבְד֣וּ אֶת־יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֥י אֹתָ֖הּ אַתֶּ֣ם מְבַקְשִׁ֑ים וַיְגָ֣רֶשׁ אֹתָ֔ם מֵאֵ֖ת פְּנֵ֥י פַרְעֹֽה׃פ
records.gloss: Not so; go, please, the men, and serve Yahweh, for it you [are] seeking. And [one] drove them out from with [the] face of Pharaoh.
pieces: Not that way! You men may go and serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; that, after all, is what you want." With that, they were driven away from Pharaoh.

L.11: Not so! Go now, the men, and serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for that is what you are seeking." And they drove them out from the presence of Pharaoh.

R.11: No! Only your men can go and worship {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. That is what you asked for anyway." Then Moses and Aaron were chased away from Pharaoh.

decisions.choice: the men: the adult males only
decisions.reason: This word means men as distinct from women and children, as in 12:37. Pharaoh refuses the little ones of verse 10; families left behind would keep the men tied to Egypt.

decisions.choice: for that is what you are seeking: Pharaoh narrows the request
decisions.reason: Pharaoh claims that a festival for the men is all they asked, though Moses has asked for "my people" (5:1; verse 3) and has just named every age (verse 9).

decisions.choice: drove them out: someone drove them out
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject; Pharaoh's servants put Moses and Aaron out.

decisions.choice: the men
decisions.reason: "Men" has no gender setting here, because adult males are specifically meant.

decisions.choice: Moses and Aaron
decisions.reason: Readable names the people driven out, and says "worship" as in verse 3.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה נְטֵ֨ה יָדְךָ֜ עַל־אֶ֤רֶץ מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ בָּֽאַרְבֶּ֔ה וְיַ֖עַל עַל־אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם וְיֹאכַל֙ אֶת־כָּל־עֵ֣שֶׂב הָאָ֔רֶץ אֵ֛ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִשְׁאִ֖יר הַבָּרָֽד׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, stretch out your hand over [the] land of Egypt for the locust[s], that it may come up on [the] land of Egypt and eat all [the] vegetation of the land, all that left the hail.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Hold out your hand over the land of Egypt to bring the locusts. They will come up over the land of Egypt and eat every plant in the country, everything the hail left standing."

L.12: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand over the land of Egypt for the locusts, that they may come up over the land of Egypt and eat every plant of the land, all that the hail has left."

R.12: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Hold out your hand over Egypt. Then locusts will come up over the land. They will eat every plant that the hail did not destroy."

decisions.choice: for the locusts: to call up the locusts
decisions.reason: Moses' raised hand is the signal for the locusts to come, as with the hail (9:22).

decisions.choice: vegetation: plants, grass and crops
decisions.reason: The word for the green plants of the field (Genesis 1:11-12, 29-30), which the hail had struck (9:22, 25).

records.heading: Locusts cover the land

records.source: וַיֵּ֨ט מֹשֶׁ֣ה אֶת־מַטֵּהוּ֮ עַל־אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַיִם֒ וַֽיהוָ֗ה נִהַ֤ג ר֥וּחַ קָדִים֙ בָּאָ֔רֶץ כָּל־הַיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא וְכָל־הַלָּ֑יְלָה הַבֹּ֣קֶר הָיָ֔ה וְר֨וּחַ֙ הַקָּדִ֔ים נָשָׂ֖א אֶת־הָאַרְבֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: And stretched out Moses his staff over [the] land of Egypt, and Yahweh drove [a] wind of [the] east in the land all that day and all the night; the morning came, and the wind of the east carried the locust[s].
pieces: So Moses held out his staff over the land of Egypt, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sent an east wind blowing over the land all that day and all that night. When morning came, the locusts were there, borne in on the east wind.

L.13: And Moses stretched out his staff over the land of Egypt, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} drove an east wind over the land all that day and all the night. [When] it was morning, the east wind had carried the locusts.

R.13: So Moses held out his staff over Egypt. And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made a wind blow from the east across the land all that day and all that night. In the morning the locusts arrived, carried in by the wind.

decisions.choice: an east wind: a hot wind from the desert
decisions.reason: A wind from the east blew in from the desert. It scorches crops (Genesis 41:6), and here it brings the locusts. An east wind also drives back the sea in 14:21.

decisions.choice: the morning came: by morning
decisions.reason: The wind blew a day and a night; by the next morning the locusts had arrived.

records.source: וַיַּ֣עַל הָֽאַרְבֶּ֗ה עַ֚ל כָּל־אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם וַיָּ֕נַח בְּכֹ֖ל גְּב֣וּל מִצְרָ֑יִם כָּבֵ֣ד מְאֹ֔ד לְ֠פָנָיו לֹא־הָ֨יָה כֵ֤ן אַרְבֶּה֙ כָּמֹ֔הוּ וְאַחֲרָ֖יו לֹ֥א יִֽהְיֶה־כֵּֽן׃
records.gloss: And came up the locust[s] on all [the] land of Egypt and settled in all [the] territory of Egypt, very heavy; before it not had been thus locust[s] like it, and after it not will be thus.
pieces: The locusts swept over the whole land of Egypt and settled throughout its territory in vast numbers. No locust swarm before it had ever been like this one, and none after it will be.

L.14: And the locusts came up over all the land of Egypt and settled in all the territory of Egypt, very heavy; before them there had not been such locusts as these, and after them there will not be such.

R.14: The locusts came over all of Egypt and landed everywhere. There were huge numbers of them. There had never been so many locusts before, and there never will be again.

decisions.choice: very heavy: dense, immense
decisions.reason: The adjective is from the root "heavy", used of Pharaoh's heart (verse 1), the heavy swarm (8:20) and the heavy hail (9:18, 24).

decisions.choice: before it and after it: never before or since
decisions.reason: A way of saying the plague was without equal. The hail was described in the same way (9:18, 24), and Joel 2:2 uses similar words of an army like locusts.

records.source: וַיְכַ֞ס אֶת־עֵ֣ין כָּל־הָאָרֶץ֮ וַתֶּחְשַׁ֣ךְ הָאָרֶץ֒ וַיֹּ֜אכַל אֶת־כָּל־עֵ֣שֶׂב הָאָ֗רֶץ וְאֵת֙ כָּל־פְּרִ֣י הָעֵ֔ץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הוֹתִ֖יר הַבָּרָ֑ד וְלֹא־נוֹתַ֨ר כָּל־יֶ֧רֶק בָּעֵ֛ץ וּבְעֵ֥שֶׂב הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה בְּכָל־אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And it covered the eye of all the land, and grew dark the land, and it ate all [the] vegetation of the land and all [the] fruit of the tree[s] which had left the hail, and not was left any green on tree[s] or on [the] vegetation of the field in all [the] land of Egypt.
pieces: They covered the face of the whole land until the land went dark. They ate up every plant in the country and all the fruit on the trees that the hail had spared. Across the whole land of Egypt, no tree and no field plant kept a single green leaf.

L.15: And they covered the eye of all the land, and the land grew dark; and they ate every plant of the land and all the fruit of the trees that the hail had left, and nothing green was left on tree or on plant of the field in all the land of Egypt.

R.15: They covered the ground until it was dark with them. They ate every plant and all the fruit on the trees that the hail had not destroyed. There was not one green leaf left on any tree or plant in all of Egypt.

decisions.choice: the land grew dark: dark with locusts
alternatives: the sky over the land was darkened
decisions.reason: The ground was black with the swarm. The words may also mean that the swarm darkened the sky over the land.

decisions.choice: the fruit the hail had left: the last of Egypt's crops
decisions.reason: The hail had struck the trees (9:25); the locusts take what remained (verse 5).

decisions.choice: the face of the land / the ground
decisions.reason: As in verse 5.

records.source: וַיְמַהֵ֣ר פַּרְעֹ֔ה לִקְרֹ֖א לְמֹשֶׁ֣ה וּֽלְאַהֲרֹ֑ן וַיֹּ֗אמֶר חָטָ֛אתִי לַיהוָ֥ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֖ם וְלָכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And hurried Pharaoh to summon Moses and Aaron and said, I have sinned against Yahweh your God and against you.
pieces: Pharaoh hastily sent for Moses and Aaron. He said, "I have sinned against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, and against you too.

L.16: And Pharaoh hurried to call Moses and Aaron and said, "I have sinned against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God and against you.

R.16: Pharaoh quickly called for Moses and Aaron. He said, "I have sinned against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, and I have sinned against you.

decisions.choice: I have sinned: I have done wrong
decisions.reason: Pharaoh confesses for the second time; after the hail he said, "I have sinned this time" (9:27). Here he admits wrong against God and against Moses and Aaron.

decisions.choice: hurried to summon: called them at once
decisions.reason: The verb shows Pharaoh's alarm; earlier he waited until a plague was well under way.

records.source: וְעַתָּ֗ה שָׂ֣א נָ֤א חַטָּאתִי֙ אַ֣ךְ הַפַּ֔עַם וְהַעְתִּ֖ירוּ לַיהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֑ם וְיָסֵר֙ מֵֽעָלַ֔י רַ֖ק אֶת־הַמָּ֥וֶת הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: And now forgive please my sin only this time, and entreat Yahweh your God that he may remove from on me only this death.
pieces: Now please forgive my sin, just this once. Plead with {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God to lift this death from me, if nothing more."

L.17: And now, forgive, please, my sin only this once, and entreat {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} may remove from me only this death."

R.17: Please forgive my sin just this one time. Pray to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. Ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to save me from these deadly locusts."

decisions.choice: this death: this deadly plague
decisions.reason: The locusts bring death by destroying the food of the land.

decisions.choice: forgive: lift, bear away
decisions.reason: The verb "lift" is used for forgiving sin (Genesis 50:17; Exodus 32:32; 34:7). "Forgive" is addressed to Moses alone, while "entreat" is addressed to both brothers.

decisions.choice: these deadly locusts
decisions.reason: Readable says what "this death" is.

records.source: וַיֵּצֵ֖א מֵעִ֣ם פַּרְעֹ֑ה וַיֶּעְתַּ֖ר אֶל־יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And he went out from with Pharaoh and entreated Yahweh.
pieces: Moses went out from Pharaoh's presence and prayed to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.18: And he went out from Pharaoh and entreated {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.18: Moses left Pharaoh and prayed to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: entreated: prayed for Pharaoh
decisions.reason: The verb of 8:4, 26. Moses prays as Pharaoh asked, as he did after the swarm (8:26) and the hail (9:33).

decisions.choice: Moses
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Moses; Literal keeps "he".

records.source: וַיַּהֲפֹ֨ךְ יְהוָ֤ה רֽוּחַ־יָם֙ חָזָ֣ק מְאֹ֔ד וַיִּשָּׂא֙ אֶת־הָ֣אַרְבֶּ֔ה וַיִּתְקָעֵ֖הוּ יָ֣מָּה סּ֑וּף לֹ֤א נִשְׁאַר֙ אַרְבֶּ֣ה אֶחָ֔ד בְּכֹ֖ל גְּב֥וּל מִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And turned Yahweh [a] wind of [the] sea very strong, and it lifted the locust[s] and thrust it into [the] Sea of Reed[s]; not remained locust one in all [the] territory of Egypt.
pieces: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} turned the wind around. A gale blew in from the west, lifted the locusts, and swept them into the Red Sea. In all the territory of Egypt not one locust remained.

L.19: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} turned [it into] a very strong sea wind, and it lifted the locusts and thrust them into the Sea of Reeds; not one locust remained in all the territory of Egypt.

R.19: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made the wind change. A very strong wind blew from the west. It picked up the locusts and blew them into the Red Sea. There was not even one locust left in Egypt.

decisions.choice: a sea wind: a west wind
decisions.reason: The Mediterranean Sea lies west of the land of Israel, so in Hebrew "seaward" means west. The wind now blows the opposite way to the east wind of verse 13.

decisions.choice: the Sea of Reeds: the sea Israel would cross, known as the Red Sea
decisions.reason: The name means "sea of reeds"; "reeds" is the word used in 2:3. The same name is used for the sea of the crossing (13:18; 15:4, 22) and for the Gulf of Aqaba (1 Kings 9:26). The Septuagint calls it the Red Sea, the name long used for it.

decisions.choice: the Red Sea
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the familiar name; Literal translates the Hebrew name, "Sea of Reeds".

decisions.choice: from the west
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the direction that "sea wind" means.

records.source: וַיְחַזֵּ֥ק יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־לֵ֣ב פַּרְעֹ֑ה וְלֹ֥א שִׁלַּ֖ח אֶת־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ
records.gloss: And made strong Yahweh [the] heart of Pharaoh, and not he let go [the] sons of Israel.
pieces: Yet {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made Pharaoh stubborn, and he did not release the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

L.20: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made Pharaoh's heart strong, and he did not let the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel go.

R.20: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made Pharaoh stubborn. So he did not let the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} go.

decisions.choice: Yahweh made Pharaoh's heart strong: as God said he would
decisions.reason: God is the subject, as he said in 4:21 and as in 9:12. See the note on 7:3.

decisions.choice: made Pharaoh stubborn
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "made strong", the Hebrew verb. Balanced and Readable say what a strong heart means here.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה נְטֵ֤ה יָֽדְךָ֙ עַל־הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וִ֥יהִי חֹ֖שֶׁךְ עַל־אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם וְיָמֵ֖שׁ חֹֽשֶׁךְ׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, stretch out your hand toward the heavens, that there may be darkness over [the] land of Egypt, and one may feel darkness.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Raise your hand toward the sky, and darkness will come over the land of Egypt, a darkness so thick that people can feel it."

L.21: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand toward the heavens, that there may be darkness over the land of Egypt, and [that] darkness may be felt."

R.21: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Hold up your hand toward the sky. Then the land of Egypt will be dark. It will be so dark that people can feel it."

decisions.choice: may be felt: a darkness so thick it can be touched
alternatives: so that people grope in the dark
decisions.reason: The verb means to feel or grope. It may mean that the darkness seemed solid, or that people had to grope their way about, as the same verb is used in Deuteronomy 28:29 of groping in darkness.

decisions.choice: no warning to Pharaoh: the ninth plague comes unannounced
decisions.reason: As with the gnats (8:12) and the boils (9:8), there is no warning. Psalm 105:28 recalls this plague first.

records.heading: Three days of darkness

records.source: וַיֵּ֥ט מֹשֶׁ֛ה אֶת־יָד֖וֹ עַל־הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם וַיְהִ֧י חֹֽשֶׁךְ־אֲפֵלָ֛ה בְּכָל־אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרַ֖יִם שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת יָמִֽים׃
records.gloss: And stretched out Moses his hand toward the heavens, and there was darkness of gloom in all [the] land of Egypt three days.
pieces: So Moses raised his hand toward the sky, and deep darkness lay over the whole land of Egypt for three days.

L.22: And Moses stretched out his hand toward the heavens, and there was a darkness of gloom in all the land of Egypt three days.

R.22: So Moses held up his hand toward the sky. Then it became completely dark everywhere in Egypt for three days.

decisions.choice: darkness of gloom: utter darkness
decisions.reason: Two words for darkness are joined to make it as dark as can be. The pair is used again in Joel 2:2 and Zephaniah 1:15.

records.source: לֹֽא־רָא֞וּ אִ֣ישׁ אֶת־אָחִ֗יו וְלֹא־קָ֛מוּ אִ֥ישׁ מִתַּחְתָּ֖יו שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֑ים וּֽלְכָל־בְּנֵ֧י יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל הָ֥יָה א֖וֹר בְּמוֹשְׁבֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: Not saw a man his brother, and not rose anyone from under him three days; and for all [the] sons of Israel there was light in their dwellings.
pieces: For three days nobody could see anybody else, and nobody stirred from where they were. But the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} all had light in their homes.

L.23: No one saw {{gender:anyone else|his brother}}, and no one rose from {{gender:their|his}} place for three days; but all the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel had light in their dwellings.

R.23: For three days no one could see anyone else, and no one moved from where they were. But there was light in all the homes of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

decisions.choice: a man did not see his brother: no one could see anyone else
decisions.reason: "Brother" here means a neighbor or anyone at all.

decisions.choice: no one rose from under him: no one moved from where he was
decisions.reason: "From under him" means from the spot where a person sat or lay.

decisions.choice: light in their dwellings: God set Israel apart
decisions.reason: As with the swarm (8:18), the livestock disease (9:4) and the hail (9:26), Israel is spared.

records.source: וַיִּקְרָ֨א פַרְעֹ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ לְכוּ֙ עִבְד֣וּ אֶת־יְהוָ֔ה רַ֛ק צֹאנְכֶ֥ם וּבְקַרְכֶ֖ם יֻצָּ֑ג גַּֽם־טַפְּכֶ֖ם יֵלֵ֥ךְ עִמָּכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And summoned Pharaoh Moses and said, go, serve Yahweh; only your flock[s] and your herd[s] will be detained; also your little ones will go with you.
pieces: Pharaoh summoned Moses and said, "Go and serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Only your flocks and herds are to be kept back; even your little ones may go along with you."

L.24: And Pharaoh called Moses and said, "Go, serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; only your flocks and your herds will be held back. Your little ones also may go with you."

R.24: Then Pharaoh called for Moses. He said, "Go and worship {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. You can even take your children with you. But your sheep, goats, and cattle must stay here."

decisions.choice: held back: detained, kept in place
decisions.reason: Pharaoh keeps the animals as a pledge that the people will come back. It is his fourth partial offer (8:21, 24; 10:11).

decisions.choice: little ones: children and dependents
decisions.reason: As in verse 10. Pharaoh now yields what he refused there.

decisions.choice: worship; sheep, goats, and cattle
decisions.reason: As in verses 3 and 9.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֔ה גַּם־אַתָּ֛ה תִּתֵּ֥ן בְּיָדֵ֖נוּ זְבָחִ֣ים וְעֹל֑וֹת וְעָשִׂ֖ינוּ לַיהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃
records.gloss: And said Moses, also you, you will give into our hand sacrifices and burnt offerings, and we will offer to Yahweh our God.
pieces: Moses said, "You yourself must even put into our hands sacrifices and burnt offerings for us to offer to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God.

L.25: And Moses said, "You yourself also must give into our hand sacrifices and burnt offerings, that we may offer [them] to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God.

R.25: Moses said, "You must also let us have animals for sacrifices and burnt offerings to offer to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God.

decisions.choice: you also will give into our hand: you must let us have animals to offer
alternatives: you yourself will even provide animals
decisions.reason: Moses may mean that Pharaoh must let them take their own animals, or, more boldly, that Pharaoh himself will even supply animals. The emphatic "you also" allows either.

decisions.choice: sacrifices and burnt offerings: the two main kinds of animal offering
decisions.reason: In a "sacrifice" part of the animal was eaten by the worshipers; a "burnt offering" was burned whole on the altar (Leviticus 1; 3). Jethro offers both in 18:12.

decisions.choice: animals
decisions.reason: Readable says what the sacrifices were.

records.source: וְגַם־מִקְנֵ֜נוּ יֵלֵ֣ךְ עִמָּ֗נוּ לֹ֤א תִשָּׁאֵר֙ פַּרְסָ֔ה כִּ֚י מִמֶּ֣נּוּ נִקַּ֔ח לַעֲבֹ֖ד אֶת־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ וַאֲנַ֣חְנוּ לֹֽא־נֵדַ֗ע מַֽה־נַּעֲבֹד֙ אֶת־יְהוָ֔ה עַד־בֹּאֵ֖נוּ שָֽׁמָּה׃
records.gloss: And also our livestock will go with us; not will remain a hoof, for from it we will take to serve Yahweh our God, and we, not we know with what we will serve Yahweh until our coming there.
pieces: Our animals are coming with us too; not a single hoof will stay behind. It is from them that we must take what we use to serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God, and until we reach the place, we ourselves cannot tell which ones we will need to serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

L.26: And our livestock also will go with us; not a hoof will be left behind, for from it we must take [some] to serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God, and we ourselves do not know with what we must serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} until we come there."

R.26: All our animals must go with us. We will not leave even one behind. We must choose some of them to use when we worship {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God. We will not know which ones we need for worshiping {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} until we arrive."

decisions.choice: not a hoof: not a single animal
decisions.reason: The hoof stands for the whole animal: nothing at all will be left.

decisions.choice: with what we will serve: what offerings Yahweh will ask for
decisions.reason: Moses does not yet know what God will require; they will sacrifice "as he tells us" (8:23).

decisions.choice: worship
decisions.reason: As in verse 3.

records.source: וַיְחַזֵּ֥ק יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־לֵ֣ב פַּרְעֹ֑ה וְלֹ֥א אָבָ֖ה לְשַׁלְּחָֽם׃
records.gloss: And made strong Yahweh [the] heart of Pharaoh, and not he was willing to let them go.
pieces: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made Pharaoh stubborn, and he would not agree to let them go.

L.27: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made Pharaoh's heart strong, and he was not willing to let them go.

R.27: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made Pharaoh stubborn. He refused to let them go.

decisions.choice: Yahweh made Pharaoh's heart strong
decisions.reason: As in verse 20. See the note on 7:3.

decisions.choice: was not willing: refused
decisions.reason: The verb speaks of the will. God's act and Pharaoh's unwillingness are stated side by side.

decisions.choice: made Pharaoh stubborn
decisions.reason: As in verse 20.

records.source: וַיֹּֽאמֶר־ל֥וֹ פַרְעֹ֖ה לֵ֣ךְ מֵעָלָ֑י הִשָּׁ֣מֶר לְךָ֗ אֶל־תֹּ֨סֶף֙ רְא֣וֹת פָּנַ֔י כִּ֗י בְּי֛וֹם רְאֹתְךָ֥ פָנַ֖י תָּמֽוּת׃
records.gloss: And said to him Pharaoh, go from me; guard yourself, not you add to see my face, for on [the] day you see my face you will die.
pieces: Pharaoh said to him, "Out of my sight! Watch yourself: do not come before me ever again. If you see my face one more time, that day you will die."

L.28: And Pharaoh said to him, "Go from me! Take heed to yourself; do not see my face again, for on the day you see my face you will die."

R.28: Pharaoh said to Moses, "Leave me! Be careful! Do not ever come back to see me. If you ever come before me again, you will die that very day."

decisions.choice: see my face: come into my presence
decisions.reason: To see a ruler's face is to be admitted to him, as Joseph says to his brothers (Genesis 43:3, 5; 44:23).

decisions.choice: you will die: a threat of execution
decisions.reason: Pharaoh threatens to have Moses put to death.

decisions.choice: Moses
decisions.reason: Readable names the person Pharaoh speaks to.

records.source: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֖ה כֵּ֣ן דִּבַּ֑רְתָּ לֹא־אֹסִ֥ף ע֖וֹד רְא֥וֹת פָּנֶֽיךָ׃פ
records.gloss: And said Moses, right you have spoken; not I will add again to see your face.
pieces: Moses said, "You are right. This is the last time I will see your face."

L.29: And Moses said, "You have spoken rightly; I will not see your face again."

R.29: Moses said, "All right. I will never come to see you again."

decisions.choice: I will not see your face again: Moses' last audience
decisions.reason: Moses' final words to Pharaoh follow in 11:4-8, in the same meeting, and he leaves "in hot anger" (11:8).

decisions.choice: you have spoken rightly: so be it, as you have said
decisions.reason: Moses accepts Pharaoh's words and turns them into his own vow.
